title: Protecting Affordable Coverage for Employees Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on September 28, 2015. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Protecting Affordable Coverage for Employees Act

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (PPACA) and Public Health Service Act to include employers with 51 to 100 employees as large employers for purposes of health insurance markets. States have the option to treat these employers as small employers. Currently under PPACA, employers with 51 to 100 employees are small employers, but before January 1, 2016, states have the option to treat them as large employers. (Under PPACA, health insurance offered in the small group market must meet certain requirements that do not apply to the large group market, including the requirement to cover the essential health benefits.)

Funds are made available to the Medicare Improvement Fund for services provided during and after FY2020.

summary.headline: This 2015 law changes how health insurance rules treat employers with 51 to 100 workers and sets aside funds for Medicare.
summary.what_it_does: It amends the Affordable Care Act so employers with 51 to 100 employees can be treated as large employers in the health insurance market, and states may choose to treat them as small employers. Before January 1, 2016, states could treat these employers as large, which would exempt their plans from the small group market rules, including the requirement to cover essential health benefits. The law also makes funds available to the Medicare Improvement Fund for services provided during and after fiscal year 2020.

who_it_affects.how: They can be classified as large or small employers for health insurance purposes, which determines which coverage rules apply to the plans they offer.

who_it_affects.group: Employees and families covered by small group health plans
who_it_affects.how: Plans offered by these employers may or may not have to include essential health benefits, depending on how their state classifies the employer.
States may choose whether to treat these employers as small or large employers for health insurance market rules.
The law makes funds available to the Medicare Improvement Fund for services provided in fiscal year 2020 and later, though the summary does not say what those funds will pay for.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted October 7, 2015; the state option to treat these employers as large applies before January 1, 2016, and the Medicare Improvement Fund funding applies to services in fiscal year 2020 and later.
